exposure: Birthweight of the first vaginally born baby
Use of forceps during delivery (yes, no)
outcome: Prevalence of sonographic anal sphincter defects
cohort: 2,818 women seen for investigation of pelvic floor disorders at a tertiary urogynecology unit between January 2014 and May 2021
finding: Forceps delivery and high vaginal parity (>5) were significant predictors of residual external anal sphincter defects on imaging in women with pelvic floor disorders.
mod_finding: The strongest risk factors for a residual anal sphincter defect were first vaginal birth and forceps delivery.
